title: Internet
text: The Internet links networks using Internet protocols and carries services including the web and email.

title: World Wide Web
text: The Web uses URLs, HTTP, and HTML to connect documents and applications over the Internet.

title: Python programming
text: Python is an interpreted language used in automation, web development, education, data work, and science.

title: SQLite
text: SQLite stores a relational database in a single file and is widely embedded in applications.

title: Computer security
text: Security reduces unauthorized access and disruption through updates, backups, access control, and strong unique passwords.

title: Algorithm
text: An algorithm is a finite procedure for solving a problem or transforming input into output.

title: Operating system
text: An operating system coordinates hardware, files, memory, processes, and interfaces for programs and users.

title: Computer network
text: Networks exchange data using communication links and agreed protocols such as TCP/IP.

title: Cloud computing
text: Cloud computing provides remotely managed storage, processing, and software services with scalable capacity.

title: Data backup
text: A backup is a separate copy of data used to restore information after loss, error, or damage.

title: Solar System
description: Sun and objects bound by its gravity.
text: The Solar System includes the Sun, eight planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids, and comets.

title: Earth
text: Earth is a rocky planet with liquid surface water, an atmosphere, and a biosphere.

title: Moon
text: The Moon orbits Earth and its changing illuminated face creates familiar lunar phases.

title: Star
text: Stars produce energy through nuclear fusion; the Sun is the nearest star to Earth.

title: Galaxy
text: A galaxy contains stars, gas, dust, and dark matter bound together by gravity.

title: Black hole
description: Region where gravity is extremely strong.
text: A black hole is a compact object whose gravity prevents light from escaping beyond its event horizon.

title: Photosynthesis
text: Plants, algae, and cyanobacteria use light, water, and carbon dioxide to make sugars and release oxygen.

title: Cell biology
description: Cells are basic units of life.
text: Cells carry out life processes; organisms may consist of one cell or many specialized cells.

title: DNA
text: DNA stores hereditary instructions in sequences of nucleotide bases and is copied during cell division.

title: Evolution
description: Change in inherited populations over generations.
text: Evolution explains how populations change through processes including natural selection, mutation, and genetic drift.

title: Climate change
text: Recent climate change is chiefly driven by greenhouse gases from human activities such as burning fossil fuels.

title: Greenhouse gases
text: Carbon dioxide, methane, and other greenhouse gases absorb infrared radiation and influence Earth's climate.

title: Renewable energy
text: Renewable energy uses sources including sunlight, wind, water, geothermal heat, and sustainable biomass.

title: Solar power
text: Solar photovoltaic cells convert light into electricity, while solar thermal systems collect heat.

title: Recycling
text: Recycling can conserve materials and energy when collection, sorting, and processing are effective.

title: Biodiversity
text: Biodiversity includes diversity within species, among species, and among ecosystems.

title: Water cycle
text: Water circulates through evaporation, condensation, precipitation, infiltration, and runoff.

title: Ocean
description: Large connected body of salt water.
text: Oceans cover most of Earth's surface and help regulate weather, climate, and the water cycle.

title: Forest
text: Forests provide habitat, store carbon, influence water cycles, and supply materials to people.

title: Air pollution
text: Air pollution can harm health and ecosystems; sources include combustion, industry, transport, and wildfires.

title: Continental drift
text: Continental drift is explained by plate tectonics, in which rigid plates move slowly over geological time.

title: Mountain
text: Mountains form through tectonic uplift, volcanism, or erosion and often influence local climate.

title: River
text: Rivers carry water from higher areas toward lakes, seas, or other rivers and shape landscapes.

title: Desert
text: Deserts can be hot or cold; low rainfall rather than temperature defines a desert.

title: Latitude
text: Latitude measures angular distance north or south of the Equator in degrees.

title: Map
text: Maps use symbols and scale to represent geographic relationships, routes, boundaries, and features.

title: Time zones
description: Regions using a common standard time.
text: Time zones coordinate civil time with Earth's rotation, commonly using offsets from Coordinated Universal Time.

title: Passport
text: A passport is an official document that identifies its holder for international travel and may enable entry requests.

title: Public transport
text: Public transport includes buses, trains, ferries, and other services available to the public.

title: Jet lag
description: Sleep disruption after rapid time-zone travel.
text: Jet lag can occur when a person's internal body clock is out of step with local time after travel.

title: History
text: History examines evidence about past events and societies to interpret change and continuity over time.

title: Ancient Egypt
text: Ancient Egypt developed along the Nile and is known for pharaohs, hieroglyphic writing, and monumental architecture.

title: Ancient Greece
text: Ancient Greek societies influenced philosophy, drama, politics, mathematics, and art.

title: Roman Empire
text: The Roman Empire was a large state centered on Rome that shaped law, languages, engineering, and governance.

title: Renaissance
text: The Renaissance was a period of renewed interest in classical learning, art, science, and humanist ideas.

title: Industrial Revolution
text: Industrialization transformed manufacturing, work, cities, transport, and economies beginning in the eighteenth century.

title: Second World War
text: World War II involved many nations and ended with Allied victory after immense human and material losses.

title: United Nations
text: The United Nations was founded in 1945 to promote peace, cooperation, human rights, and development.

title: Democracy
text: Democracy is a system in which political power is exercised by citizens directly or through elected representatives.

title: Rule of law
text: Rule of law means laws are publicly known, applied consistently, and bind governments as well as people.

title: Constitution
text: A constitution sets basic principles, institutions, powers, and rights for a political community.

title: Election
text: An election is a process through which voters choose people or decide questions in public office.

title: Civil rights
text: Civil rights protect individuals from unequal treatment and support participation in social and political life.

title: Tax
text: Taxes fund public services and government operations; tax systems vary by jurisdiction and income type.

title: Inflation
text: Inflation reduces the purchasing power of a unit of currency when prices rise over time.

title: Interest rate
description: Cost of borrowing or return on saving.
text: An interest rate expresses interest paid or earned as a percentage over a stated period.

title: Budget
text: A budget estimates income and expenses and helps households, organizations, and governments plan resources.

title: Personal finance
description: Managing household money and financial decisions.
text: Personal finance covers budgeting, saving, debt, insurance, taxes, retirement planning, and investing according to a person's goals and circumstances.

title: Compound interest
text: Compound interest adds earned interest to principal, so later interest is calculated on a growing balance.

title: Stock market
text: Stock markets allow investors to buy and sell shares representing ownership interests in companies.

title: Insurance
text: Insurance pools risk: policyholders pay premiums and insurers may cover specified losses under agreed terms.

title: Nutrition
text: Nutrition concerns nutrients that provide energy, building materials, and regulation for the body.

title: Human heart
text: The human heart pumps blood through the circulatory system, delivering oxygen and nutrients while carrying away carbon dioxide and other wastes.

title: Physical exercise
text: Regular physical activity can support cardiovascular fitness, strength, mobility, mood, and general health.

title: Sleep
text: Sleep supports restoration, learning, memory, and regulation of many body processes.

title: Hand washing
text: Washing hands with soap and water removes many microbes and can reduce transmission of infections.

title: Vaccine
text: Vaccines expose the immune system to a safe representation of a threat to build protective immune memory.

title: Mental health
text: Mental health affects thinking, feeling, coping, relationships, and daily functioning; professional support can help.

title: First aid
description: Initial assistance during illness or injury.
text: First aid is immediate care before professional treatment; emergencies require local emergency services.

title: Hydration
text: Hydration describes adequate water balance, which supports normal temperature control and body functions.

title: Medicine
text: Medicine applies evidence, prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation to support health.

title: Public health
text: Public health protects and improves community health through prevention, policy, research, and services.

title: Painting
text: Painting creates images or expression on a surface using color, line, texture, and composition.

title: Music
text: Music combines elements such as rhythm, melody, harmony, timbre, and form.

title: Photography
text: Photography records or creates images by capturing light with chemical film or electronic sensors.

title: Architecture
text: Architecture combines technical, social, environmental, and aesthetic considerations in the design of built environments.

title: Literature
text: Literature includes fiction, poetry, drama, essays, and other writing read for ideas, language, and experience.

title: Novel
text: A novel is a long work of prose fiction, often exploring characters, setting, plot, and themes.

title: Poetry
text: Poetry uses rhythm, imagery, sound, and line to create expressive or imaginative writing.

title: William Shakespeare
text: William Shakespeare wrote plays and poems in early modern English; his works remain widely performed and studied.

title: Library
description: Collection and access service for information.
text: Libraries collect, organize, preserve, and provide access to books, media, and information resources.

title: Museum
text: Museums collect, conserve, interpret, and display objects of artistic, scientific, historical, or cultural importance.

title: Physics
text: Physics studies motion, forces, energy, matter, space, and time using observation and mathematical models.

title: Chemistry
text: Chemistry studies matter, its properties, composition, and transformations in chemical reactions.

title: Atom
description: Basic unit of a chemical element.
text: An atom has a nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons.

title: Gravity
text: Gravity is the attraction between objects with mass and governs orbits, falling objects, and large-scale structure.

title: Electricity
text: Electricity includes electric charge, current, voltage, circuits, and electromagnetic effects.

title: Scientific method
text: Scientific inquiry develops questions, hypotheses, observations, tests, analysis, and revisable explanations.

title: Mathematics
text: Mathematics investigates patterns, numbers, shapes, change, logic, and abstract structures.

title: Probability
text: Probability expresses how likely an event is, usually using a number from zero to one.

title: Statistics
text: Statistics collects, summarizes, analyzes, and interprets data while accounting for uncertainty.

title: Measurement
text: Measurement compares a quantity with a standard unit to communicate size, amount, time, or other properties.

title: HTML
text: HTML gives web documents structure with elements for headings, paragraphs, links, images, and forms.

title: CSS
text: Cascading Style Sheets control presentation such as layout, colors, spacing, and responsive display.

title: JavaScript
text: JavaScript adds behavior and interactivity to web applications and also runs in server and tooling environments.

title: URL
text: A URL identifies a resource and commonly includes a scheme, host, path, query, and fragment.

title: Domain Name System
text: DNS translates domain names into information such as IP addresses used to reach network services.

title: Encryption
text: Encryption transforms readable data into ciphertext so authorized parties can recover it using a key.

title: Two-factor authentication
text: Two-factor authentication requires two different proofs, such as a password and a device code, to sign in.

title: Version control
text: Version control records file changes so people can compare versions, collaborate, and recover earlier work.

title: Open-source software
description: Software with source available under a license.
text: Open-source licenses allow source code to be inspected, used, modified, and shared under stated conditions.

title: Keyboard shortcuts
text: Keyboard shortcuts use keys or key combinations to perform commands quickly without navigating menus.
